mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impact.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) over a 3-month period signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input shortages and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 55% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) that exceeds 7% signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand, which will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board measure) rises by > 5 points during the signal period, indicating a disconnect between labor market and consumer spending trends.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise by more than 10% year-over-year and the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals a housing-led demand boom that will boost S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: early-cycle recovery with easy monetary policy
failure_condition: Housing affordability index (NAR) falls below 100 during the signal period, indicating that rising mortgage rates are offsetting the demand boost from low FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening yield curve (10y-2y spread < 1%) combined with a rising core CPI (CPIAUCSL) signals a tightening monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Fed cuts rates by > 50bps during the signal period, signaling a policy pivot that reverses the tightening impulse.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200,000 jobs per month for 3 consecutive months and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals a tight labor market that will boost wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 200k for 3 months and UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: Average hourly earnings (BLS) growth slows by > 0.5pp during the signal period, indicating that labor market tightness is not translating into wage gains.

mechanism_narrative: Real estate loans (RSAFS) growing faster than 10% year-over-year signals a credit-fueled demand boom that will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: High-yield credit spreads (BofA index) widen by > 100bps during the signal period, indicating a credit crunch that offsets the demand boost from rising real estate loans.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the ISM manufacturing PMI (> 55) combined with a flattening yield curve (10y-2y spread < 1%) signals a supply chain bottleneck that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input shortages and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, indicating that the supply shock is not significantly impacting equity prices.
